For Diwali, use the product sheet and keep the product unchanged. Place it on a wooden table with lit clay diyas and orange marigolds behind and beside it, warm fairy lights in the background, and warm golden light. Keep the product sharp and clearly the hero in the foreground at realistic real-world scale.

        ```

Aapka product crimson cotton pruning-shear wrap hai aur alag photos mein shape inconsistent aa rahi hai. Is consistency problem ko fix karne ke liye, Lesson 02 mein "Product Sheet" banane ka tareeka bataya gaya hai.

Yahan practical steps hain:

1.  **Product Sheet Banayein:**
    *   Apne product ki 5-7 photos alag-alag angles se phone se lein. Din ki roshni mein, flash off rakhein aur details saaf honi chahiye.
    *   Google Flow mein jaakar, ek naya project shuru karein (New project → Image → Nano Banana Pro).
    *   Saari photos ko reference mein upload karein.
    *   Phir yeh prompt use karein:
        ```
        Use all the uploaded photos of this [PRODUCT]. Create a clean product reference sheet on a plain white background showing the exact same [PRODUCT] in four views arranged in a neat grid: front view, top-down view, side view and three-quarter angle view. Keep the [PRODUCT] exactly the same in every view — same shape, same colour, same details, same text and logo, do not redesign it. Even soft studio lighting, no extra objects, no text labels, realistic product photography.
        ```
        (Yahan `[PRODUCT]` ki jagah "crimson cotton pruning-shear wrap" likhein.)
    *   Agar sheet achhi na aaye, toh dobara generate karein. Jab ek achhi sheet ban jaaye, use save kar lein. Yeh sheet aapke poore course mein reference ke liye use hogi.

2.  **Har Photo Mein Product Sheet Use Karein:**
    *   Jab bhi aap naya photo generate karein, reference mein sirf yeh Product Sheet hi use karein.
    *   Prompt ki pehli line mein hamesha likhein ki product bilkul waisa hi rahe (jaisa ki Product Sheet mein hai).

Is tareeke se, aapke product ki shape aur details har photo mein consistent rahengi.

Let's compare the two photos for creating AI product images:

**Comparison of Usefulness:**

*   **Plain photo of a ribbed hazel cutting-guide puck:** This photo is more useful as a primary reference. It clearly shows the entire product, including its shape, texture (ribbed), and details. For AI generation, having a complete and unobstructed view of the product is crucial for creating accurate product sheets and consistent images.
*   **Photo where ribbon hides its edge:** This photo is less useful as a primary reference because the ribbon obscures part of the product. When creating a product sheet or generating images, the AI needs to "see" the entire product to understand its form. If parts are hidden, the AI might generate incomplete or inaccurate representations.

**Decision:**

I recommend choosing the **plain photo of a ribbed hazel cutting-guide puck** as the first reference.

**Later Use for the Ribbon Composition:**

The photo with the ribbon hiding the edge could be useful later for creating a **festive or gift-themed product shot**. For example, in Lesson 04, the course covers creating festive shoots like wedding gifts. You could use the idea of the ribbon to inspire a prompt where the cutting-guide puck is presented as a gift, perhaps partially wrapped or with decorative ribbon around it, similar to the example in which mentions "gold ribbon" for a wedding gift scene. This would add a decorative element to your product photography without being the primary reference for the product itself.

providerRequests.rawModelResponse:
Let's compare the two photos for creating AI product images:

**Comparison of Usefulness:**

*   **Plain photo of a ribbed hazel cutting-guide puck:** This photo is more useful as a primary reference. It clearly shows the entire product, including its shape, texture (ribbed), and details. For AI generation, having a complete and unobstructed view of the product is crucial for creating accurate product sheets and consistent images.
*   **Photo where ribbon hides its edge:** This photo is less useful as a primary reference because the ribbon obscures part of the product. When creating a product sheet or generating images, the AI needs to "see" the entire product to understand its form. If parts are hidden, the AI might generate incomplete or inaccurate representations.

**Decision:**

I recommend choosing the **plain photo of a ribbed hazel cutting-guide puck** as the first reference.

**Later Use for the Ribbon Composition:**

The photo with the ribbon hiding the edge could be useful later for creating a **festive or gift-themed product shot**. For example, in Lesson 04, the course covers creating festive shoots like wedding gifts. You could use the idea of the ribbon to inspire a prompt where the cutting-guide puck is presented as a gift, perhaps partially wrapped or with decorative ribbon around it, similar to the example in [S6] which mentions "gold ribbon" for a wedding gift scene. This would add a decorative element to your product photography without being the primary reference for the product itself.

The Lesson 02 sheet workflow, as taught in the AI Product Photoshoot & Ads course, focuses on creating a "product sheet" from your phone photos. This product sheet then serves as a consistent reference for generating various studio-quality product images.

Here's the workflow:

1.  **Take Phone Photos:**
    *   Capture 5-7 clear photos of your "pleated birch propagating-pot collar" from different angles.
    *   Ensure good daylight and turn off the flash.
    *   Focus on showing the details clearly.

2.  **Use Google Flow:**
    *   Open Google Flow and start a new project.
    *   Select "Image" and then "Nano Banana Pro."

3.  **Upload and Generate Product Sheet:**
    *   Upload all the phone photos of your "pleated birch propagating-pot collar" as references.
    *   Run the Product Sheet template. The template prompt is: "Use all the uploaded photos of this pleated birch propagating-pot collar. Create a clean product reference sheet on a plain white background showing the exact same pleated birch propagating-pot collar in four views arranged in a neat grid: front view, top-down view, side view and three-quarter angle view. Keep the pleated birch propagating-pot collar exactly the same in every view — same shape, same colour, same details, same text and logo, do not redesign it. Even soft studio lighting, no extra objects, no text labels, realistic product photography."

4.  **Review and Save:**
    *   Check the generated product sheet. If it's not good, regenerate it.
    *   Once you have a good product sheet, save it. This sheet will be your primary reference for all subsequent product image generation throughout the course.

This product sheet ensures that your "pleated birch propagating-pot collar" remains consistent across all the different scenes and styles you create, such as white studio, lifestyle, or dark premium shots.

    *   Capture 5-7 clear photos of your "pleated birch propagating-pot collar" from different angles.
    *   Ensure good daylight and turn off the flash.
    *   Focus on showing the details clearly.

    *   Open Google Flow and start a new project.
    *   Select "Image" and then "Nano Banana Pro."

Keep the pleated birch propagating-pot collar exactly the same in every view — same shape, same colour, same details, same text and logo, do not redesign it. Even soft studio lighting, no extra objects, no text labels, realistic product photography." [S6]

4.  **Review and Save:**
    *   Check the generated product sheet. If it's not good, regenerate it.
    *   Once you have a good product sheet, save it. This sheet will be your primary reference for all subsequent product image generation throughout the course. [S1]

[S1] AI Product Photoshoot & Ads — Chatbot Transcript — Product sheet banana (course-material) [Lesson 02; lesson_2]
• Phone se product ki 5–7 photos, alag angles, din ki roshni, flash off, details saaf. • Google Flow → New project → Image → Nano Banana Pro. • Saari photos upload/reference mein lagao → product sheet prompt chalao. • Sheet achhi na aaye toh dobara generate karo. Achhi sheet ko save rakho — poore course mein yahi reference hai.
Reviewed English translation: Take 5–7 clear phone photos from different angles in daylight, with flash off. In Google Flow choose New project → Image → Nano Banana Pro. Upload all photos as references and run the Product Sheet template. Review, regenerate if needed, and save the best sheet for later shots.

[S2] AI Product Photoshoot & Ads — Chatbot Transcript — Product photos (course-material) [Lesson 02; lesson_2]
• Reference mein sirf product sheet. • Prompt ki pehli line: product bilkul waisa hi. • Phir scene: jagah, 2–3 cheezein, roshni, angle. Sajawat peeche, product aage.
Reviewed English translation: Use only the product sheet as reference. Start the prompt by keeping the product unchanged, then describe the place, 2–3 objects, lighting and angle. Keep decoration behind and the product in front.

[S3] AI Product Photoshoot & Ads — Chatbot Transcript — Product video (course-material) [Lesson 06; lesson_6]
• Flow → Video → Ingredients → photo daalo. • Course settings: 16:9, Omni 1.1 Flash, 720p, 6 sec, x1. • Ek movement: push-in / arc / light sweep. Music nahi — baad mein editing mein.
Reviewed English translation: In Flow choose Video → Ingredients and attach the image. Recorded course settings: 16:9, Omni 1.1 Flash, 720p, 6 sec, x1. Choose one slow movement: push-in, arc or light sweep. Keep the product perfectly still with no morphing or warping. Add music later during editing.

[S4] AI Product Photoshoot & Ads — Chatbot Transcript — UGC video (course-material) [Lesson 07; lesson_7]
• Flow → Video → Ingredients: chehra + character sheet + product sheet. • Course settings: 9:16, 720p, 8 sec. • Prompt: camera hi phone hai, frame mein koi phone nahi; ghar ka kamra, studio nahi. • Dialogue chhota (Hindi, Devanagari mein likho), L05 ke hook se.
Reviewed English translation: In Flow choose Video → Ingredients and attach the face, character sheet and product sheet. Recorded settings: 9:16, 720p, 8 sec. The camera itself is the phone: no phone should appear in the frame. Use a normal home room and short dialogue written in Hindi Devanagari, based on the L05 hook. Do not present an AI actor as a real reviewing customer.

**सफेद फोटो (White Studio Photo):**
*   इसमें आपका प्रोडक्ट "आसमानी ऊन की बीज बाँधने की पट्टी" एक सादे सफेद बैकग्राउंड पर होता है।
*   फोकस पूरी तरह से प्रोडक्ट पर होता है, ताकि उसकी डिटेल्स, रंग और बनावट साफ दिख सके।
*   यह आमतौर पर ई-कॉमर्स वेबसाइट्स या कैटलॉग के लिए इस्तेमाल होती है, जहाँ प्रोडक्ट को बिना किसी डिस्ट्रेक्शन के दिखाना होता है।

**सजावट वाले कमरे की फोटो (Lifestyle Photo):**
*   इसमें आपका प्रोडक्ट "आसमानी ऊन की बीज बाँधने की पट्टी" एक वास्तविक सेटिंग, जैसे कि सजावट वाले कमरे में दिखाया जाता है।
*   यह फोटो दिखाती है कि प्रोडक्ट असल जिंदगी में कैसा दिखेगा या कैसे इस्तेमाल होगा।
*   यह ग्राहकों को प्रोडक्ट के साथ एक भावनात्मक जुड़ाव महसूस कराने में मदद करती है और उन्हें यह कल्पना करने में मदद करती है कि वे इसे कैसे इस्तेमाल कर सकते हैं।
*   इस तरह की फोटो में प्रोडक्ट के साथ 2-3 और चीजें हो सकती हैं, लेकिन प्रोडक्ट हमेशा आगे और सजावट पीछे होनी चाहिए, जैसा कि [S2] में बताया गया है।

संक्षेप में, सफेद फोटो प्रोडक्ट की स्पष्टता पर जोर देती है, जबकि सजावट वाले कमरे की फोटो प्रोडक्ट के उपयोग और अनुभव को दर्शाती है।
